title: PrivVPC: IAM policy generator + upgrade playbook for least-privilege Terraform modules
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create a reusable Terraform module and an operator-facing upgrade playbook that programmatically generates least-privilege IAM/RBAC policies for Private (VPC) deployments, plus automated health-checks and a safe rollout path. The goal is to reduce manual policy drift, enable automated upgrades of RBAC bindings across clusters/accounts, and provide clear rollback and observability for any IAM changes.
technical_notes: Design a generator that ingests a service-to-action mapping (YAML/JSON) and produces provider-specific policy statements (AWS IAM, GCP IAM bindings, Azure RBAC). The Terraform module should: 1) expose variables for principal types (service, user, role), 2) support policy document templating (HCL + jsonencode), 3) optionally create granular inline policies vs managed policies, 4) output metadata for drift detection. Implement a CI job that runs 'terraform plan' + policy linting and a staged apply workflow (canary accounts, region mirroring). Health checks: create a /private-iam/health endpoint in control-plane orchestration that verifies binding replication, token-based test calls for each service, and a KV cache check for eventual consistency. Use terraform state tags to mark module version and last-applied hash to detect manual drift.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Terraform module publishes a stable interface: variables, outputs, and example usage for AWS/GCP/Azure.
2) Policy generator can emit least-privilege statements for three canonical services (runtime, runtime-metrics, kv-cache) with scoped resources and documented rationale.
3) CI pipeline runs policy-lint and rejects unsafe wildcard actions with an auditable failure message.
4) Upgrade playbook documents canary rollout to 2 staging accounts and an automated health-check pass criteria.
5) Rollback path is codified: terraform state rollback + reapply previous policy module version.
6) Monitoring: dashboard shows last-apply time, failed health checks (>0 triggers pager), and drift detected count.
7) Security review sign-off recorded in PR and Confluence doc.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (staging): in two staging VPC accounts, run generator to create policies for runtime and metrics; apply via gated CI with manual approval. Phase 2 (canary): select two low-traffic customer VPCs, apply changes with 30-minute observation windows and automated health checks. Phase 3 (global): batch remaining customers in groups of 10, with automatic rollback if health-check failures exceed threshold. Include an operator CLI: redwood-iam upgrade --target <account|group> --dry-run to preview plan. Notify via Slack channel #priv-deploy-iam on every apply and rollback.
test_plan: Unit tests for policy generator templates, integration tests that spin a sandbox VPC (in CI) and assert that tokens can call runtime endpoints with least-privilege credentials. Add chaos tests where a binding is removed to ensure health-check detects and triggers alert. End-to-end test: full canary apply in ephemeral infra with terraform destroy at end. Maintain a matrix of AWS/GCP/Azure providers in CI with mocked credentials for non-destructive validation.
monitoring: Create console dashboard tile: 'Priv IAM Policy Health' showing last_apply_timestamp, drift_count, failing_bindings, and recent_health_check_logs. Alerts: PagerDuty on >3 failing_bindings or any failed canary health check. Wire logs to existing infra-syslog and to the 'private-deploy' long-term retention stream for audits.
